kurz: The peels and cores of tart apples are full of pectin. Simmered out and reduced, they become a natural setting agent.
bild_im_kopf: Like paste from the craft cupboard: unremarkably runny, but it holds together what would not hold on its own.
dauer: 1 day, of which 1½ hours of work
ergebnis: About 500 ml of pectin juice (as a guide).
haltbarkeit: A week in the fridge; frozen in portions, many months.
material: 1–1.5 kg tart apples, or peels and cores (e.g. from apple cake, collected in the freezer)
a cold plate for the test
verwendung: For jam from low-pectin fruit such as strawberries, cherries or pears: about 250 ml per 1.5 kg of fruit (as a guide).

schluesselmomente.schritt: Chop the apples roughly, cover with water and simmer, covered, for 40–60 minutes
schluesselmomente.warum: Heat releases the [[pektin|pectin]] from the cell walls into the water.

schluesselmomente.schritt: Let it drip through a cloth overnight; do not squeeze
Reduce the juice by half, uncovered
Plate test: let a spoonful with a little sugar and lemon cool on a cold plate
schluesselmomente.warum: If it sets and wrinkles when pushed, there is enough pectin. Otherwise reduce further.
